title: A study to look at the clinical, human and economic effects on patients who suffer prolonged epileptic seizures
official: The clinical, humanistic and economic patient burden of prolonged seizures in epilepsy: a prospective observational study in the UK (RWE1597)
summary:
Background and study aims 
The study is designed to look at patients who suffer from prolonged seizures (PS) in epilepsy.  The study will collect information on the clinical effects (medical outcomes), human effects (effects on everyday life) and economic effects (effects on ability to work) in this group of patients.  

Who can participate? 
Patients aged at least 12 years old who suffer from PS

What does the study involve? 
Patients will be asked to complete questionnaires (three times over a 6-month period) and study diaries capturing seizures for 6 months. These will be completed electronically on a phone or tablet. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
There are no benefits from taking part, but the study may collect information which is useful in the treatment of this group of patients in the future.  

Where is the study run from? 
UCB Biopharma SRL (Belgium)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
September 2026 to September 2027

Who is funding the study? 
UCB Biopharma SRL (Belgium)

Who is the main contact? 
Fiona McNulty, fiona.mcnulty@ubc.com

interventions.name: Observational study including questionnaires and patient diaries. Patients will receive usual care. Patients will be asked to complete questionnaires (three times over a 6-month period) and study diaries capturing seizures for 6 months. These will be completed electronically on a phone or tablet.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Is at least 12 years old at the time of providing assent/consent for study participation
2. Has a documented medical diagnosis of epilepsy
3. Is at risk of prolonged seizures (PS) according to the REST definitions based on physician’s clinical impression of seizure history and disease status
4. Has had at least one PS event within the last month prior to study enrolment evaluation
5. Patient has sufficient cognitive ability to understand the Patient-Reported Outcome questionnaires and seizure diary items and to provide their own answers. Patients may receive non-directive assistance limited to technical or physical support (e.g., typing or navigating the device), provided that all response content is generated by the patient
6. Informed consent and, where applicable, assent for participation will be obtained in accordance with applicable national regulations and the procedures approved by the Ethics Committee
7. The patient, and caregiver/LAR if applicable, has sufficient command of English language to understand the study information and requirements
Exclusion criteria:
1. Is enrolled in any clinical trial at the time of assent/consent for study participation
2. Has a history of presence of known non-epileptic seizures which cannot be distinguished from qualifying epileptic seizures
